title: devbin_canon.bats hides the canon sweep's output, so a CI red there cannot say what it saw (one Ubuntu flake at v3.2.4)
body:
`tests/unit/devbin_canon.bats`, test `canon: a clean estate exits 0`, runs `bin/.devbin/cmd/canon` in the real checkout and asserts only `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`. When that assertion fails the runner prints nothing but the assertion line, so a red there cannot say whether canon found a divergence (exit 1) or lost a control (exit 2), nor which path it named.

Measured at the v3.2.4 tag (f89b8285b), GitHub run 39031497031. Attempt 1 (the tag push, 2026-10-17 12:10:40Z): job `Test on Ubuntu` failed test 175 with only `(in test file unit/devbin_canon.bats, line 37)` and `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]' failed`; the test took 1.2 s. Job `Test on macOS` passed the same test at the same tag. Attempt 2 (a re-run of the failed jobs at 12:28Z): every job green, test 175 ok at 12:31:58Z after 3.9 s. So the red was not deterministic.

What it was not: canon has not changed since e91131d92 (2026-09-25) and was green on the Ubuntu leg at 7bfca4e7a; the only inputs that changed between that green and the tag are the issue records 0606.json and 0607.json, both LF with a trailing newline and accepted by prettier; the same sweep run read-only on an Ubuntu checkout at c9d2b2e58 (585 records, 0606 present) is green. The cause of the one red is unmeasured, and this issue does not claim one.

Remedy: make the test speak. On a non-zero status print `$output` before failing, so the next red names the divergence or the control that died, for example `[ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2; return 1; }`. The second assertion on the controls line stays as it is. Where the output then names a path, that path is the next issue; where it names a control, the control is.
